CVE-2026-125350.title: Update Chrome and restart it
CVE-2026-125350.why: Google fixed a flaw hackers are already using. A booby-trapped web page could run code inside your browser. Fixed Nov 9, 2026: you need version 157.0.8103.50 or newer.
CVE-2026-125350.source: Google security advisory, Nov 9, 2026; BleepingComputer, Nov 10, 2026

edge.title: Update Edge and restart it
edge.why: Microsoft fixed the same flaw hackers are using in Chrome. A booby-trapped web page could run code inside your browser. Edge updates itself, but only finishes after a restart.

chromebook.title: Update your Chromebook and restart it
chromebook.why: Google fixed a flaw hackers are already using in the browser built into Chromebooks. A booby-trapped web page could run code on it.

other-chromium.title: Update Brave, Opera or Vivaldi
other-chromium.why: These browsers are built on Chrome, which has a flaw hackers are already using. Install your browser's latest update and restart it.

CVE-2026-124194.title: Update Outlook
CVE-2026-124194.why: Hackers are using an Outlook flaw that can let something risky happen without asking you first. Install the latest Office update.
CVE-2026-124194.source: Microsoft Security Update Guide, Nov 10, 2026; CISA, added Nov 10, 2026
CVE-2026-124194.fixed: Office LTSC 2024 16.0.17932.21140, Office LTSC 2021 16.0.14334.21048, or newer; Microsoft 365 apps: the Nov 10, 2026 security update

CVE-2026-96951.title: Run Windows Update and restart
CVE-2026-96951.why: Hackers are using a Windows flaw to get around a built-in security protection. The fix comes through Windows Update.
CVE-2026-96951.source: Microsoft Security Update Guide, Oct 13, 2026 (KB5127648, KB5126657); CISA, added Oct 13, 2026

CVE-2024-27834.title: Make sure your Apple devices are up to date
CVE-2024-27834.why: An older Apple and Safari flaw is now being used by hackers. If your iPhone, iPad or Mac is on the latest version, you're already protected.
CVE-2024-27834.source: CISA, added Nov 4, 2026; Apple security notes, May 13, 2024
CVE-2024-27834.fixed: iOS and iPadOS 17.5 (16.7.8 on older models), macOS Sonoma 14.5, Safari 17.5, watchOS 10.5 and tvOS 17.5, or anything newer

CVE-2024-10441.title: Update your Synology drive
CVE-2024-10441.why: Hackers are using a flaw in Synology's software to take over drives remotely. Install the latest update from the drive's Control Panel.
CVE-2024-10441.source: CISA, added Nov 18, 2026; Synology advisory SA-24:20

items.title: pCloud says hackers hit its password manager
items.if_affected: If you use pCloud Pass: pCloud says a cyberattack exposed a small number of users' emails and someone tried to log in. It says stored passwords stayed encrypted and pCloud's cloud storage wasn't affected. It warns of phishing asking for your Master Password or recovery words.
items.source: The Hacker News, Nov 28, 2026

items.title: Air Force cloud system reported hacked
items.if_affected: If you work for or with the Air Force: Reuters reports hackers got into its main cloud system, which runs personnel, pay and logistics apps. It's not known whether any data was taken. The Air Force says it doesn't comment on specific systems.
items.source: Reuters, Nov 27, 2026

items.title: Business software maker SAP confirms a cyberattack
items.if_affected: If your employer runs SAP business software: SAP confirmed a cyberattack and says it found no sign that customers' business data was accessed. Nothing for you to update.
items.source: BleepingComputer, Nov 26, 2026

items.title: Hackers claim they took 166M USA Today records
items.if_affected: If you have a USA Today account: a hacker group claims it took 166M records. No breach is confirmed. Expect fake account or payment emails; the FTC says to contact companies through a number or website you know is real.
items.source: Forbes, Nov 26, 2026

items.title: Boston Scientific says hackers took some personal data
items.if_affected: If Boston Scientific sends you a breach letter: hackers tricked staff by phone and downloaded data in May. The company says Social Security numbers and financial details weren't included, and its medical devices and remote monitoring weren't affected. It says to be wary of messages urging quick action.
items.source: California Attorney General breach list (Boston Scientific notice), Nov 25, 2026

items.title: See's Candies says stolen files reached the dark web
items.if_affected: If See's Candies sends you a breach letter: hackers hit its network in April and posted some stolen files with personal details on the dark web. See's offers free Experian monitoring and says never give personal details in reply to messages about it.
items.source: California Attorney General breach list (See's Candies notice), Nov 25, 2026

items.title: Todoist says hackers took some users' emails
items.if_affected: If you use the Todoist to-do app: a hack exposed emails, scrambled passwords and sign-up dates for about 6% of customers. Todoist asked those affected to reset their password and change it anywhere else they used the same one.
items.source: TechCrunch, Nov 25, 2026

items.title: 1Password says hackers took customer names and emails
items.if_affected: If you use 1Password: a hack exposed some customers' names, emails and account details. 1Password says vaults and passwords are safe and you don't need to update anything. It warns of fake invite or account recovery emails and says it will never ask for your password or Secret Key.
items.source: 1Password, Nov 25, 2026; BleepingComputer, Nov 25, 2026; TechCrunch, Nov 25, 2026

items.title: Allstate's website and app have been down for days
items.if_affected: If you have Allstate insurance: its website and app have been down since Nov 23. Allstate hasn't said why. It says it is still handling claims by phone and at local offices, and you won't lose coverage or pay late fees if the outage blocks a payment.
items.source: TechCrunch, Nov 25, 2026

items.title: Treasury's financial crimes office says it was breached
items.if_not: A Treasury system banks use to report suspicious activity, not your devices. Nothing to update. FinCEN says someone got unauthorized access to some of its systems and it took some offline as a precaution. It hasn't said what data was reached.
items.source: The Register, Nov 25, 2026; The Hacker News, Nov 25, 2026; Nextgov/FCW, Nov 25, 2026

items.title: Barclays says hackers took card applicants' SSNs
items.if_affected: If you applied for a Barclays credit card (it issues many store and travel cards): hackers broke into its application-status site and took names, contact details, birth dates and Social Security numbers. Barclays says existing accounts weren't affected. It's offering those it writes to free Experian identity monitoring.
items.source: California Attorney General breach list (Barclays Bank Delaware notice), Nov 24, 2026

items.title: Best Egg loan site hacked; SSNs and bank numbers taken
items.if_affected: If you have a Best Egg loan: hackers got into its Financial Health site and took some customers' names, birth dates, Social Security numbers and the bank account number used for loan payments. Best Egg says it hasn't seen fraud on accounts and offers free Experian identity monitoring.
items.source: California Attorney General breach list (Best Egg notice), Nov 24, 2026

items.title: Unclassified CIA system reported hacked
items.if_not: A spy agency's unclassified research system, not your devices. Nothing to update. The CIA declined to comment.
items.source: CyberScoop, Nov 24, 2026

items.title: Chrome fixes a critical flaw; restart to finish
items.if_affected: Not a hack. Google fixed a critical Chrome flaw and hasn't said anyone is using it. Google's fix is Chrome 158.0.8127.88 on computers and 158.0.8127.92 on Android. Chrome updates itself; check Settings › About Chrome and restart if it asks.
items.source: Chrome Releases blog, Nov 23, 2026

items.title: GL.iNet routers hacked through its cloud service
items.if_affected: If you have a GL.iNet router or KVM box: GL.iNet says hackers used its GoodCloud remote service to put malware on some devices. It says to install the latest security firmware for your model from the device's admin page.
items.source: GL.iNet security notices, Nov 20, 2026 (updated Nov 23); BleepingComputer, Nov 22, 2026

items.title: Software checkout firm says card numbers were stolen
items.if_affected: If you got a letter from Cleverbridge, which runs checkout for some software sellers: hackers copied card numbers, expiry dates and security codes. Cleverbridge says to check your statements and ask your card issuer about a new card. It never asks for card details by email, phone or text.
items.source: Cleverbridge incident update, Nov 2026; BleepingComputer, Nov 2026

items.title: FBI police database reported hacked
items.if_not: A law enforcement database, not your devices. Nothing to update. Real FBI agents never call demanding money; hang up on anyone who does.
items.source: CNN via BleepingComputer, Nov 20, 2026; FBI IC3 PSA I-091726, Sep 17, 2026

items.title: Cheap no-name TV boxes used in record ad fraud
items.if_affected: If you have a cheap, uncertified no-name Android TV box: it may be one of the boxes used for ad fraud. Roku, Fire TV, Apple TV, Chromecast and name-brand TVs aren't part of it. Google says to check a box is Play Protect certified, and the FBI says to consider disconnecting suspicious devices.
items.source: FBI IC3 PSA on BADBOX 2.0, Jun 5, 2025; HUMAN Security via MarTech Cube, Nov 19, 2026

items.title: Chase says a vendor leak exposed emails
items.if_affected: If you bank with Chase: hackers got some names and emails held by marketing vendors. Chase says its services weren't disrupted. Nothing to update. Expect fake Chase emails; open the Chase app yourself instead of tapping links.
items.source: BleepingComputer, Nov 2026; ABC News, Nov 19, 2026; Gray News (KOLD), Nov 19, 2026

items.title: Synology fixes two critical flaws in its home drives
items.if_affected: Not a hack: Synology hasn't said anyone is using these flaws. It says to update DSM to 7.4.1-90080-2 or 7.3.2-86009-6 or newer (Control Panel › Update). On DSM 7.1 and BeeStation, where no full fix is out yet, Synology says to turn off the OAuth Service package.
items.source: Synology security advisories SA-26:21 and SA-26:20, Nov 19, 2026 (updated Nov 26)

items.title: Hackers got into a USDA farm payment system
items.if_affected: If you get USDA farm payments: hackers got into a USDA payment system. Nothing to update. Check any message about your account with your local office.
items.source: Nextgov/FCW, Nov 2026; DTN, Nov 24, 2026

items.title: Apple Pay, iCloud and the App Store went down
items.if_affected: An outage after a bad update at Apple, not a hack. Nothing to update on your devices. Ignore texts or calls saying your Apple ID is locked and asking for a code.
items.source: Apple statement via TechCrunch, Nov 17, 2026; AP via ABC7, Nov 17, 2026

items.title: Bank and airline outages, Nov 12–17
items.if_affected: Banks, Schwab, United and the FAA all had outages. Every company that gave a cause blamed a technical fault, not an attack. An outage doesn't move your money. If you get a call or text 'fixing' your account, hang up and call the number on your card.
items.source: Associated Press via PBS NewsHour, Nov 16, 2026; FOX 4 News (FOX Television Stations), Nov 17, 2026

items.title: Microsoft 365 down for almost 24 hours
items.if_affected: An outage, not a hack. Nothing to update. Ignore emails asking you to "restore" your mailbox.
items.source: Microsoft incident MO1550821, via BleepingComputer, Nov 12, 2026

items.title: Black Friday scam texts and fake stores
items.if_affected: Not a hack, just scam season. Texts about a missed delivery or a redelivery fee are fake: track packages in the store's own app. No real company asks you to pay with gift cards. Forward scam texts to 7726.
items.if_not: Nothing to update. Delivery scam texts are everywhere this season; forward them to 7726.
items.source: Massachusetts Office of Consumer Affairs, Nov 10, 2026

items.title: U.S. warns of hacks on store freezers
items.if_not: Commercial refrigeration in grocery stores and cold storage, not home fridges.
items.source: Reuters, Nov 5, 2026; FBI and CISA warning via BleepingComputer, Nov 5, 2026

items.title: Android's November update fixes a no-tap flaw
items.if_affected: Google fixed a serious flaw that needs no tap from you. Hackers aren't using it yet. Install the update when your phone offers it and check the security patch level says November 5, 2026 or later.
items.source: Android Security Bulletin, November 2026 (published Nov 2, 2026)

items.title: $6.3 billion stolen from Binance
items.if_affected: If you use Binance: the exchange says it refilled affected wallets. Ignore messages offering refunds or asking you to "verify" your account.
items.source: FBI cyber alert, Nov 2026; TRM Labs, Oct 30, 2026

items.title: Google Cloud outage in London
items.if_not: Hit UK banks and services. Backup power failed; nothing for you to update.
items.source: Google Cloud Service Health, Oct 20, 2026; Technology Magazine, Oct 2026
